topic: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra: should agents use a cheaper model?
caption:
Would you use your most expensive AI model just to fill out a form?

OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Terra on October 26. It focuses on visual understanding and computer use, with standard API prices 50% lower than GPT-5.6 Terra.

What interests me as a developer isn't another model leaderboard. It's how we build agents.

A useful agent can spend dozens of steps reading screens, entering data, checking results, and navigating tools. Running a frontier reasoning model for every step may not be the best tradeoff.

OpenAI reports that Terra scored 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at maximum reasoning, versus GPT-5.6 Terra's published 21.5%. But Sol and Astra remain better choices for the hardest coding tasks.

My takeaway: choose the model based on the task, not the hype. An efficient model might handle routine UI work, while complex or consequential actions deserve stronger reasoning and human approval. Of course, cheaper tokens don't automatically mean cheaper successful tasks.

Would you build a multi-model agent that escalates difficult steps, or keep one powerful model throughout the workflow?

Source: https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-terra/
